summary: Steel tower in the Northumberland Forest, reportedly brought down after a 1991 climb; its cab was reported at a Port Hope fire museum.

facts.status_note: Brought down after a 1991 climb; the cab is reported at the Canadian Fire Fighters Museum in Port Hope, which is temporarily closed.

access.note: The Fire Hall Museum list marks the Canadian Fire Fighters Museum as temporarily closed. No source I read says whether the cab is on display today.

events.note: Hikers climbed the Northumberland Forest tower on 11 May 1991, according to a 2013 blog post. The blog is the only source for the climb.

notes_for_editor: The cab's identity rests on a 2013 blog post (it says the cab on the museum lawn was the tower climbed in 1991) and on the Forest Rangers site, which places the Northumberland Tower at the museum. The brought-down date is not given anywhere; the blog reports it second-hand. The 1991 climb site is not identified in the blog, so the firelookout.ca address is the only location; the sources do not say whether the 1991 tower stood at that address. The Rice Lake island claim conflicts with the Baltimore record and the Port Hope cab and is not explained. The Fire Hall Museum listing is undated. The Museums Ontario listing returned HTTP 522 and the www page 404, so the museum's current status is unconfirmed. A search snippet quoted a Tripadvisor note that the museum has permanently closed; unverified and not used. A 1960 map entry 'Haldimand Tower (aka Northumberland), 80 ft' seen only in a search snippet came from a Southern Ontario Fire Towers Map page that returns HTTP 403; not used. No photos with a clear licence were found.
